about: v0.5b interface strings (OWNER: WP-D): Nala's bridge and the court-recital finale (view-setu.tsx, view-bookend.tsx); keys setu.*. Rules: notes/sa-ui.md.

setu.help.en: Tap a stone to turn it. Make the bridge whole.
setu.help.sa: शिलां स्पृश, सा परिवर्तते। सेतुं पूर्णं कुरु।
setu.help.ctx: Nala's bridge: how to play (परि+वृत् परिवर्तते: it turns round; a stone that sits true stays put)

setu.hintSay.ctx: Nala's bridge: after 'Ask Nala' — the stone he points at is marked (the first one, in day order, not yet true)

setu.whole.en: The bridge is whole! It reaches Laṅkā.
setu.whole.ctx: Nala's bridge: every stone sits true (the shore meets Laṅkā); ▶ continues the story

setu.ask.ctx: Nala's bridge: hint button (A) — Nala points at a stone

setu.stone.ctx: Nala's bridge: a stone's screen-reader name — stone n is day n's span ({$y} = 14, 20, 21, 22, 23 yojanas, Yuddha 6.22.66–70)

setu.set.ctx: Nala's bridge: a stone's state when it sits true (screen reader; feminine, agrees with शिला)

setu.yojanas.ctx: Nala's bridge: under each stone, the yojanas built that day (Yuddha 6.22.66–70)

setu.days.ctx: Nala's bridge: caption over the five stones — one stone for each day of building

setu.built.ctx: Nala's bridge: yojanas standing so far (the days whose stone sits true) of the hundred (Yuddha 6.22.74)

setu.shore.ctx: Nala's bridge: the left end, the shore the army stands on

setu.lanka.ctx: Nala's bridge: the right end, the far shore (Laṅkā)

setu.endAll.ctx: Kathā ending screen (finale): heading over all 21 verses with their state
